q: Why does moving `l` right when the sum is too small never skip the answer?
options: Because the array has no duplicates
nums[l] plus the largest remaining value is still too small, so nums[l] can't be in any answer
It can skip it, you need a second pass
why: Every partner left for nums[l] is ≤ nums[r], and even nums[r] wasn't enough. So nums[l] is safely discarded.

q: Two pointers from both ends on a sorted array of n numbers takes…
why: Each step moves one pointer inward by one, and they stop when they meet: at most n steps.

q: The array is unsorted and you need all triplets summing to 0. First step?
why: Sorting (O(n log n)) makes two pointers valid and makes skipping duplicates easy. The total stays O(n²).

q: In Container With Most Water, which pointer moves?
why: The shorter line caps the height. Keeping it while narrowing can only lose area, so it's the one to drop.

q: What does this return for s = "racecar"?
why: Mirrored characters match all the way to the middle.

q: 3Sum with sort + fix one element + two pointers runs in…
why: n choices for the fixed element, each followed by an O(n) two-pointer scan. Sorting's O(n log n) is smaller.
